name: fig-07
title: Nested cellular hierarchy

purpose.mechanism: The cell's structural composition as a place graph — extracellular matrix, membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, organelles — with the processes that act across levels.

config.caption: The cell's structural composition as a place graph — extracellular matrix, membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, organelles — with the processes that act across levels.

Time series of the runnable fig07 hierarchy (fig07-runnable): six ODE processes act on stores up to SIX levels deep in one place graph and feed each other, so the whole cell evolves as one coupled system. Transmembrane transport fills the cytoplasmic nutrient pool; metabolism makes metabolites + energy; transcription reads the deeply-nested DNA into RNA; translation makes protein; subunit assembly grows the ribosome pool (closing the loop); replication holds DNA at its genome set point. The cascade propagates across every level — the nested hierarchy of coupled processes running together. From scripts/build_fig07_dynamics.py.

question: How do nested composites build a structural hierarchy?
